appraisal_events.evidence: Seule Mme Verdurin, quand elle parlait à Odette, ne faisait pas que faillir et se trompait exprès [in calling her Mme de Crécy]; and: Vous ne savez pas arranger les chrysanthèmes.
appraisal_events.explanation: Even as a guest in Odette's own salon, Mme Verdurin deliberately withholds full recognition of Odette's married name and criticizes her taste, preserving her own dominance over her former protégée.

appraisal_events.evidence: Mme Verdurin disait avec dégoût à son mari: « Charmant milieu! Il y avait toute la fleur de la Réaction! » though the narrator states her own salon was not even at the stage of incubation of the great gatherings to come.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator ironically exposes Mme Verdurin's satisfied belief that she has glimpsed aristocratic society at Odette's as self-deception, since her own salon's real ascent has not yet begun.

appraisal_events.evidence: Toute déchéance acceptée a pour conséquence de rendre les gens moins difficiles...; c'était l'âge aussi où Swann...se plaisait à entendre dire à Mme Bontemps que c'est ridicule de ne recevoir que des duchesses...concluant...que c'était une bonne femme, très spirituelle et qui n'était pas snob.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator directly attributes Swann's newfound tolerance for Mme Bontemps's vulgar remarks to a general decline in discernment brought on by his own social fall, a judgment he would not have made in his Verdurin days.

appraisal_events.evidence: On enviait Mme Cottard que la Patronne appelait par son prénom.
appraisal_events.explanation: Mme Verdurin's use of Mme Cottard's first name marks her as singled out for special intimacy within the clan, a distinction visibly envied by the other women present.

status_effects.explanation: Despite her advancement into a grander social world, Odette remains subject to Mme Verdurin's deliberate, condescending refusal to fully grant her new married identity and taste.
The narrator quietly ridicules Mme Verdurin's inflated pride in what she takes to be Odette's aristocratic circle, revealing it as a self-flattering illusion.
Swann's once-discriminating taste is shown to have coarsened, as he now finds a vulgar woman's platitudes charming, a change the narrator explicitly frames as decline.
Being addressed familiarly by first name marks Mme Cottard's admission into a closer circle of intimacy with Mme Verdurin, a distinction the other women visibly envy.
